#### Description
Calculate an estimate of the capacity of the strategy backtest/live trade. This will provide funds with an understanding of the maximum dollar allocation they can make to the strategy to maximize its return potential without moving the market.

- Implements `AssetsUnderManagementCapacityManager`
- Adds an instance of `AssetsUnderManagementCapacityManager` in the result handlers to include AUM Capacity to algorithm statistics
- Adds "AUM Capacity" entry to `ExpectedStatistics` of regression algorithms with a considerable amount of orders.

Performance test over 10 executions of RegressionAlgorithm (5433 trades):
`master` :: Mean: `7.71` Std: `0.16`
`new` :: Mean: `7.853` Std: `0.22`
Speed decrease of 1.85%.

#### Related Issue
Closes #3539
This pull request was created on top of #3571

Include statistics that can be used to improve algorithms.

No.

issue_context.title: Implement AUM Capacity Estimate Calculation
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Calculate an estimate of the capacity of the strategy backtest/live trade. This will provide funds with an understanding of the maximum dollar allocation they can make to the strategy to maximize its return potential without moving the market.

#### Actual Behavior
No estimate available

#### Potential Solution
Capacity will be calculated using the volume capacity per symbol per trade each day. At the end of the day, the symbol capacity will be calculated as the minimum of all individual trade capacities for the specific symbol. Then, the portfolio capacity for the day will be the sum of all individual symbol capacities. The final AUM Capacity will be displayed as the average of all of the daily capacities calculated).

Please see the excel sheet for a detailed calculation of this in various circumstances.
[Alpha Capacity Calculations.xlsx](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/files/3552416/Alpha.Capacity.Calculations.xlsx)

review_comments: A comment here describing _why_ we're using `0.025m` and `0.050m` -- in fact, I'm not sure I understand what these factors mean.
This factor is the maximum percentage of market volume that is tradeable. These values are ad-hoc defined by research.
out of curiosity, what required these algorithm changes?

I'm wondering if there's any concern about silently breaking existing algorithms by changing the temporal behavior as to when this event is raised. I say this will silently break algorithms since it likely won't raise an error but rather would end in the algorithm tracking state incorrectly thereby silently corrupting the algorithm's state. _If_ this is a concern, then perhaps a _new_ event would be warranted, something like `NewOrderEventProcessed` (comments on event naming below in `<nit>`).

``` xml
<nit severity='low' type='naming-conventions' scope='events'>
```
unrelated to this PR -- `NewOrderEvent` is a **really really** _**really**_ bad event name. [Event names](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamicsax-2012/developer/naming-conventions-delegates-and-event-handlers) should be verbs as either present tense (*ing, such as `OrderSubmitting`) and denote that the event was raised _right before_, so in this case, `OrderSubmitting` implies the event handler is invoked _before_ the order is actually submitted. Following completion of submitting the order, another event would be called `OrderSubmitted`. These past tense verbs imply that the described event has been completed.

`NewOrderEvent` is ambiguous. Is this a new order event was _initialized_ -- or was it _received_, or was it _processed_ or was it _something else_ ? It appears it is intended as not just a new order event, but actually a new _fill_ or _partial fill_ event. I think a better name for the event _as-is_ on `master` would be `OrderFillProcessing`  and this new event would be `OrderFillProcessed`

Making things even more ambiguous, the documentation for `NewOrderEvent` only states:
``` csharp
/// <summary>
/// Event fired when there is a new <see cref="QuantConnect.Orders.OrderEvent"/>
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>Will be called before the <see cref="SecurityPortfolioManager"/></remarks>
```
which doesn't even mention that the event is only raised for fill/partial fill `OrderEvent` instances.
``` xml
</nit>
```

We (@Martin-Molinero and I) have discussed this. `NewOrderEvent` is a recent feature and it was only consumed by `OrderBasedInsightGenerator`, so we choose to refactor `OrderBasedInsightGenerator` instead of creating a new event (ref. #3571).
Thanks for the reference -- not just for me, but for posterity 😄

I feel like this _shouldn't_ be required... and if a callback is causing modification of a list that raises an exception _somewhere_ than I suspect we're doing something else wrong and this may just be a bandaid.
This might make a nice extension method -- I can see this being applicable in many places. I like it!

Nice tests! 👍 
I think one test case that is missing, and would be nice to have, is for the same date, the same symbol, two trades and assert it uses the minimum trade capacity of both trades?

maybe a note here saying that we're only adding the consolidator for the first config -- also, should there be preference of trades over quotes or vice versa? Right now we're just depending on whatever order the provider returns them in which (may) cause non-determinism later (perhaps)?
